events.title: Black Tuesday Stock Market Crash
events.description: The New York Stock Exchange collapsed as panicked investors sold roughly 16 million shares in a single day, wiping out billions of dollars in market value. It followed the sharp declines of Black Thursday five days earlier.
events.significance: Black Tuesday is regarded as the most devastating day in U.S. stock market history and a pivotal moment in the onset of the Great Depression, which reshaped global economic policy and led to major financial regulation.

events.title: Execution of Sir Walter Raleigh
events.description: English explorer, courtier, and writer Sir Walter Raleigh was beheaded in London's Old Palace Yard under a suspended sentence for treason dating from 1603, after his final expedition to Guiana failed and angered Spain.
events.significance: Raleigh's death marked the end of the Elizabethan age of adventurers and is remembered as a symbol of the shifting politics of James I's reign and early English colonial ambitions in the Americas.

events.title: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey
events.description: The Grand National Assembly of Turkey formally proclaimed the Republic, and Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was elected its first president, following the abolition of the Ottoman sultanate in 1922 and the Turkish War of Independence.
events.significance: The proclamation created the modern secular Turkish state and began sweeping political, legal, social, and cultural reforms that transformed the former Ottoman heartland.

events.title: First Message Sent over ARPANET
events.description: At UCLA, student programmer Charley Kline sent the first host-to-host message over ARPANET to the Stanford Research Institute. The system crashed after the letters 'lo' of the intended word 'login' were transmitted.
events.significance: This first transmission on the precursor to the internet is considered a foundational moment in the history of digital networking and global communications.

events.title: Galileo Spacecraft Flies by Asteroid Gaspra
events.description: NASA's Galileo probe, en route to Jupiter, made the first close flyby of an asteroid, passing within about 1,600 kilometers of 951 Gaspra and returning detailed images.
events.significance: The encounter provided the first close-up views of an asteroid and greatly advanced understanding of the composition and geology of small solar system bodies.
